free_tier.stated: Per-file 20 MB on free accounts, 2 GB on paid. No published account total: 'Generally, there is no limit on how many files you can upload.' HubSpot's own catalog does not state a storage figure.

retention.stated: request-rate: 100 req / 10 s / app and 250,000 / day per account on Free ('Privately distributed apps, Free and Starter, 100/app, 250,000/account'). Retention: none documented — files persist until deleted

egress.terms: Free, Cloudflare-fronted. `hubfs` files are served publicly with `Accept-Ranges: bytes`, `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, `Cache-Control: s-maxage=2592000`.

tooling: Files API (`POST /files/2026-09/files`, multipart), public URL in the response's `defaultHostingUrl` / `url`. Python/Node SDKs. No rclone backend.
chaining: 20 MB/file x unlimited files x unlimited free HubSpot accounts. Weak on its own; becomes usable only at portal scale or if you can get onto 2 GB/file.
limits_note: per-object-cap: 20 MB per file on free tools (the binding constraint by a wide margin); the docs note 'If a file is 1 GB or more, you may experience issues'. request-rate: 100 req / 10 s / app and 250,000 / day per account on Free ('Privately distributed apps, Free and Starter, 100/app, 250,000/account'). Retention: none documented — files persist until deleted. Download URLs can 429 if the rate limit is exceeded.
reliability_note: The API is genuinely good (2e5 calls/day, 100/10s) but the 20 MB free per-file cap means shard-only. HTML/JS files are served as text/plain on default domains, so binaries only.

evidence.proved: 'Files up to 20 MB for accounts with only access to HubSpot's free tools. Files up to 2 GB for accounts with paid subscriptions.'
'Generally, there is no limit on how many files you can upload.'
probe: GET -> 200, 5,123 bytes, real PNG 288x288; Range: bytes=0-99 -> 206, 100 bytes

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
